result.instructions:
opentide: Spec-driven development for agentic detection engineering. opentide gives every detection an ontology and a taxonomy, so it stays threat-aligned, maintainable and fast to ship, with or without agents.

The catalogue is YAML in the repository: threats (objects/threats/), objectives (objects/objectives/) and rules (objects/rules/). A rule's detection_model is an objective UUID; an objective lists threat UUIDs.

Workflow:
1. Search. search (keyword, UUID, technique) and coverage find what exists; get_chaining shows threat -> objective -> rule.
2. Draft. Start from opentide://templates/{object_type}, check fields against opentide://schemas/{object_type} and opentide://vocabularies/{name}, and write the file with your own tools: this server does not write files.
3. Validate until clean. Call validation_report with file or uuid after every edit. Each issue has code, severity, message, object_uuid, path, line and column (1-based), help, and fix ({safe, edits}: each edit replaces the text from (line, column) up to (end_line, end_column) with replacement). Apply safe edits as they are: they only respell the same word; check the others against help. explain(code) says what a code means. Repeat until ok is true. While drafting a query, validate_query checks it offline in its platform's language, with no tenant.
4. Preview. deploy_rule with dry_run true shows the deployment; nothing is sent.

People review and merge changes and run real deployments. Call deploy_rule with dry_run false only when a person asks for it. validate_query with live true contacts the tenant with the configured credentials: ask first. run_query with live true runs a read-only query on a tenant and returns its rows: ask first as well.

Results may carry next_actions: [{tool, arguments, command, reason}], the next call to make (command is the same step as an opentide command line). Read the reason before following one.

  "meaning": "A value is not in the vocabulary its field uses.",
  "markdown": "# vocab_unknown

A value is not in the vocabulary its field uses.

Severity: error. Reported by `opentide validate` (schema check).

## Example

```yaml
metadata:
  tlp: clearr          # tlp::1.0 has clear, green, amber, amber+strict, red
```

## How to fix

Use a value from the vocabulary the label names. When a close value exists, `help` names it and `fix` carries the edit; the edit is marked `safe` only when the two spell the same word (they differ in case, spaces, `-` or `_`) and hold no digit, so an ATT&CK id is never replaced unreviewed. The opentide VS Code extension completes vocabulary values (`opentide setup vscode` recommends it).
"
}

  "markdown": "# kql_unknown_table

The table is neither one the engine knows for the platform nor one the workspace declares in visibility.toml: a warning under Sentinel, whose workspaces hold tables no catalog lists; an error under Defender's advanced hunting schema. Declaring it in visibility.toml makes it known.

Reported by the analysis engine in a KQL query, at the place in the query: as an error, a query the platform would reject, by `opentide validate` (its `queries` check) and `opentide validate query`; as a warning or a note, style, by `opentide lint` (its `queries` check). An editor running `opentide lsp start` shows both.

## Example

```text
opentide validate query
```

## How to fix

Change the query where the frame points, then run `opentide validate query` (`--file` for one rule or query file) or `opentide lint --check queries` again. The [KQL reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/kusto/query/) describes the syntax and the commands the engine checks against.
"
}

  "found": true,
  "code": "invalid_ref",
  "meaning": "A reference names an object that does not exist.",
  "markdown": "# invalid_ref

A reference names an object that does not exist.

Severity: error. Reported by `opentide validate` (schema check).

## Example

```yaml
detection_model: 00000000-0000-4000-8002-DEADBEEF0000   # no such objective
```

## How to fix

Point the field at an object that exists: `detection_model` takes an objective or signal UUID (`opentide info objectives`), `objective.threats` and `threat.chaining[].vector` take threat UUIDs (`opentide info threats`). When the value is close to the name of an object, `help` names that object's UUID. A reference field is also a vocabulary field, but a dangling value is reported once, under this code.
"
}
